skill.name: azure-containerregistry-py
skill.description: Guides Python developers through Azure Container Registry SDK tasks for repositories, tags, manifests, authentication, downloads, and cleanup.
skill.summary: Use the Python Azure Container Registry SDK to inspect and manage container images, tags, and manifests.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, inline SDK method names, documented Azure URLs, endpoint configuration, and visible file output examples. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, hidden execution, or malicious network behavior was found. The residual concern is destructive registry deletion guidance that should include explicit safety controls.

remediation.issue: Delete examples can remove registry artifacts from live environments.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation, dry-run output, allow-listed registry names, and required backups before repository, tag, manifest, or cleanup deletion examples.

remediation.issue: The blob download example writes to a fixed local file name.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to choose a safe output path and check for existing files before writing downloaded layers.

7. **Check manifest.tags** before deleting to avoid removing tagged images

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Registry Operations Need Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents repository, manifest, tag, and cleanup deletion flows without an explicit confirmation or dry-run pattern. Running these examples against production could remove container images.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable Python workflows for Azure Container Registry images and metadata. This skill provides focused SDK examples for authentication, listing, updates, downloads, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install and configure the Azure Container Registry Python package.
Demonstrates Entra ID authentication with DefaultAzureCredential.
Lists repositories, tags, and manifest metadata with ordering options.
Updates repository and manifest write or delete permissions.
Deletes repositories, tags, manifests, and untagged old manifests.
Downloads manifests and layer blobs with sync and async client examples.
limitations: It does not provision Azure registries or identities.
It does not validate permissions or production safety for your environment.
Delete examples can remove images when executed against a live registry.
It does not include full error handling, retries, or logging patterns.

use_cases.title: Inspect Registry Inventory
use_cases.description: List repositories, tags, and manifests before maintenance or reporting.

use_cases.title: Protect Production Images
use_cases.description: Set repository and manifest flags that block writes or deletes for critical images.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Old Artifacts
use_cases.description: Find old untagged manifests and prepare a controlled deletion workflow.

prompt_templates.title: List Repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, show me the Python steps to authenticate with Entra ID and list repositories in Azure Container Registry.

prompt_templates.title: Review Image Tags
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain how I can list tags for one repository and sort them by last updated time.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dry-run plan to identify untagged manifests older than 30 days, then explain the checks before deletion.

prompt_templates.title: Build Async Inventory Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an async Python workflow that lists repositories and recent manifests, closes clients correctly, and explains where to add retries.

output_examples.input: I need to list repositories in an Azure Container Registry.
output_examples.output: The response explains package setup, endpoint configuration, Entra ID authentication, and repository iteration with the Python SDK.

output_examples.input: I need to remove stale untagged images.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a cutoff date, tag checks, digest based deletion, and a review step before running changes.

output_examples.input: I need to download a layer blob for inspection.
output_examples.output: The response describes downloading the manifest and blob, choosing an output path, and checking file handling before writing.

best_practices: Use Entra ID and least privilege roles for registry access.
Run cleanup logic in dry-run mode before deleting artifacts.
Delete by digest and check tags to avoid removing active images.
anti_patterns: Running delete examples against production without approval or backups.
Using broad credentials when read-only access is sufficient.
Saving downloaded blobs over existing files without checking the path.

faq.question: Does this skill manage Azure Container Registry from Python?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on the Azure Container Registry Python SDK for repositories, tags, manifests, downloads, and cleanup.

faq.question: Does it create a registry?
faq.answer: No. It assumes an existing registry endpoint and valid Azure authentication.

faq.question: Which authentication method is shown?
faq.answer: It recommends Entra ID through DefaultAzureCredential and also shows anonymous access for public registries.

faq.question: Can it delete images?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include repository, tag, manifest, and old untagged manifest deletion. Confirm targets before running them.

faq.question: Does it support async code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an async client pattern and shows client and credential cleanup.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written as guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
